properties.title: Special Weather Statement issued November 10 at 4:17AM CST by NWS Corpus Christi TX
properties.description:
At 417 AM CST, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm near
Gregory, or 7 miles northeast of Portland, moving northeast at 35
mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 40 mph and pea size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor damage to outdoor objects is
possible.

Locations impacted include...
Portland, Rockport, Taft, Ingleside, Aransas Pass, Gregory,
Bayside, Palm Harbor, Copano Village, Key Allegro, Corpus Christi
North Beach, Downtown Corpus Christi, Fulton and Taft Southwest.

This includes the following highways...
Interstate 37 near mile marker 1. US Highway 181 between mile markers
630 and 648.
properties.instruction:
Monitor the weather situation closely and be alert for threatening
weather conditions.

properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. Most flood related deaths occur
in automobiles. Do not attempt to cross water covered bridges, dips,
or low water crossings. Never try to cross a flowing stream, even a
small one, on foot. To escape rising water find another route over
higher ground.

Even 6 inches of fast-moving flood water can knock you off your feet
and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at midnight CST.
